IfMatch.description: The order version the caller read. A lifecycle command without it is refused rather than applied blind.
IfMatch.name: If-Match

TransitionResponse.description: The VendorOrder that moved, with the ParentOrder's re-derived aggregate state.

CreateOrderRequest.description: Accepts only the approved fingerprint the client is committing to. It accepts no price, fee, discount, funding split, vendor id, branch id or payment reference: every one of those is authority the server resolves from the approved quote.

OrderLine.description: Immutable item snapshot. A later catalogue rename, repricing or delisting never changes what this purchase said.

ParentOrder.description: One customer commerce purchase, created exactly once from one approved quote.

payment_operation_ref.description: Bound by a later payment-capable section. Section 17E never accepts it from a request and never executes a payment.

platform_allocations.description: Parent-scope allocation rows that belong to no single vendor: the platform's own fee and tax.

receiver_snapshot.description: Delivery contact evidence only. It never becomes a customer account.

ParentOrderState.description: Derived from the VendorOrders. PARTIALLY_COMPLETED is reported when every allocation is terminal but they did not all end the same way, so a mixed outcome is never hidden.

VendorOrder.description: One financially and operationally isolated vendor/branch allocation. Every money field is this vendor's own share; none is a gross customer figure.

delivery_other_funded_minor.description: Delivery benefit funded by an approved source that is neither the vendor nor the platform. Kept separate so a subsidy is never misreported as platform money.

info.description: Durable order orchestration from an approved Section 17D quote. One customer purchase becomes one ParentOrder and one financially and operationally isolated VendorOrder per vendor/branch allocation. This surface creates no payment operation and moves no money.
info.title: Vendor Service Section 17E ParentOrder and Multi-Vendor VendorOrders
